trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted Finance customer information involving at least 500 consumers. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; data counts as unencrypted if the key was also accessed
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery. Discovery is the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent of Finance other than the person committing the breach (314.4(j)(2)). Holding company staff running Finance's shared services should be treated as Finance's agents for this clock
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov. Content: Finance's name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any law enforcement delay determination

trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days of discovery and must include the determination and a way to contact the official. Law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request

obligation: Qualified Individual report to Finance's Board of Managers
trigger: Security events and management's responses are material matters for the annual report
deadline: In the next annual written report (each September); the Finance President is also told the same day under POL-03

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the covered entity (holding company to subsidiary)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the holding company maintains for a subsidiary (for example email, files, HRIS, SFTP) involving that subsidiary's personal information
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. The agent must give the covered entity all information it needs for its notices. POL-03 requires same-day internal notice
notify: The affected subsidiary's President (covered entity); the agent may send the (3) and (4) notices on its behalf (501.171(6)(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the holding company processes personal information for each subsidiary under the intercompany services agreement

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents: name with SSN, government ID number, financial account number with access code, and other listed elements; or user name or email with password
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Law enforcement may delay notice by written request (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents (employees of any group company; Finance borrowers and applicants)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each group company is the covered entity for its own employees and customers

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (a Finance breach could reach this count)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected employees or borrowers who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency; most borrowers and employees are Florida residents

trigger: Unsecured PHI of the group health plan involved. The sponsor holds enrollment information for the plan; the 164.530(k) relief for fully insured plans covers 164.530(a)-(f) and (i) only, not the breach notification rule
deadline: Individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (164.404)
notify: Plan participants; HHS; coordinate with the insurance carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Possibly - counsel decides whether plan PHI was involved and who notifies

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA

obligation: Bank notice of suspected payment fraud or credential compromise
trigger: Fraudulent or suspicious payment; compromise of a bank portal user or of the SFTP server
deadline: Immediately on suspicion; recall requests are time-critical
notify: Bank fraud line and relationship manager

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

trigger: Event the credit agreement treats as requiring notice (counsel to confirm the covenant wording)

citation: Merchant agreements (contract); Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1.1
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data at Supply or Home Services
deadline: Per merchant agreement (time not set in this sample). Whatever the agreement says, Visa's rules require the compromise to be reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation, through the processor (What To Do If Compromised v10.0, A.1.1)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data may be involved (unlikely: terminals are point-to-point encrypted and online payments use the processor's hosted page)
verified: n/a (contract term not set); true (Visa clock)

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not an SEC registrant (P03 section 1)

trigger: Notification incident at a bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining a notification incident occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a bank holding company (P03 section 1)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then); recheck applicability when final

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
